newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index edges cautiously up at noon.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index edges cautiously up at noon.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index eked out light gains at midday on Wednesday with investors nervous about aftershocks from government policies to cool the markets, analysts said.
The foreign currency B index edged up 0.14 points or 0.09 percent to 151.21 on turnover of HK$68.6 million.
"Today's technical rally was limited by the A share falls which in turn was weighed down by uncertainty over government policies," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
The domestic currency A share index slid 3.07 points or 0.70 percent to 437.41 on turnover of 3.3 billion yuan.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) has set up two special phone lines for investors to report irregularities and illegal trading on the stock markets, state media said on Wednesday.
"The phone lines are no big deal, but people see them as another government jab against stock speculation," an analyst at a western investment bank said.
Beijing began to impose new measures to rein in stock speculation at the start of May, at which time the A and B indices had surged more than 50 percent from the beginning of 1997.
Shenzhen Health Mineral Water Co Ltd was the sharpest gainer in the B share market, adding HK$0.17 or 5.14 percent to HK$3.48.
